meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so you have about twenty minutes. Before you say anything else, tell me who entered that zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before he saw it on his phone in the middle of class.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, and "the zero stands" isn't a basis. On what evidence, and under which part of your school's procedure, because 4.2 says you call me before a mark goes in, and nobody called me. Answer that, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Okay. I'm writing down October 15 and the outline; show me the outline, and show me the exact line you say isn't in Hamlet, Hale. And students change their argument between an outline and a final draft all the time, so what else do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn and an apology, and I want to see the October 15 outline and the exact line you say is not in Hamlet. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see both documents for herself.
What moved her: Apologising for the brush-off and then naming a dated outline and a specific misquotation earned a small sign of ground, because both are tied to Owen's own work and she could check them.
What cost ground: Opening by refusing to talk and declaring the mark final with no basis, because it confirmed her fear that the school decided first and would explain later.
Try next time: When she first asked who entered the zero and whether Owen was heard, own entering it before calling home in one sentence, then turn the screen and show her the outline and the misquoted line right away.
